summary: Section O/P/Q (Phase C) end-to-end testing on Laravel 11 CRM. Created /app/backend/tests/test_section_opq.py with 15 pytest tests covering payment milestones + collections dashboard + aging + allotment auto-issue + AFS lifecycle (draft->send_for_sign->signed->registered) + demand letters (interest calc 18% p.a., delivery, escalation) + full RBAC (postsales.manage). ALL 15/15 tests PASS in isolation. Frontend verified via Playwright: nav-collections + nav-demands present, Collections page renders collections-cards + aging-buckets + collections-overdue, Demands page shows demands-tbody with demand-row-{id}, Post-Sales tab renders 5 milestone rows with ms-pay buttons + working pay modal (ms-amount/ms-method/ms-ref/ms-pay-save), ps-gen-afs button drafts an AFS + renders agreement-{id} with afs-send-{id}, demand-{id} rows show dm-post/dm-esc buttons, allotment letter auto-appears at 10% collection.

minor.issue: throttle:20,1 is aggressive — the full pytest suite (5 test files, ~90 tests) exhausts the limit and yields 429s when run back-to-back. Not an app bug, but consider raising to throttle:60,1 for dev or exempting local IPs.

critical_code_review_comments: PaymentScheduleService::checkAllotment is called on every syncStatuses (i.e. every GET /bookings/{id}/milestones and after every payment). PostSalesService::generateAllotment must remain idempotent — verified via test_allotment_idempotent. Fine as long as the guard `where('type','allotment')` stays in place.

DemandLetterService::generateForMilestone auto-delivers via 'whatsapp+email' at creation time — no explicit delivery step is required, but the docstring implies POST /deliver is the delivery trigger. Slight semantic mismatch; consider decoupling so /deliver is the sole channel toggle.

AgreementService::serial() and DemandLetterService::serial() both use COUNT+1 within the year without a transaction — same race-condition risk as PaymentService::receiptNo() flagged in iter5. For MVP this is fine, but add a unique index + retry loop before prod.

$milestone->due_at->diffInDays(now()) always returns a positive number in Carbon 3, but relies on isPast() gating; if this codepath ever runs against a not-yet-past date (regression), days_overdue would be misleading. Consider `max(0, ...)` guard.

success_rate.backend: 100% (15/15 Section O/P/Q; regression 82/89 with 7 rate-limit-induced flakes)

seed_data_creation: Ran `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed --force` before Section OPQ test run. Tests self-provision fresh leads/bookings using UUID-based unique phones/emails (TEST_OPQ_ prefix). Overdue milestones are created via `php artisan tinker --execute=...->update(['due_at'=>now()->subDays(45)])` from within the test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public URL https://deal-flow-platform.preview.emergentagent.com is NOT wired to Laravel (proxied to a FastAPI backend that returns {detail:'Not Found'}). ALL testing was against the local Laravel server at http://127.0.0.1:8000. Playwright browser automation successfully reached 127.0.0.1:8000 from within the container. When running the full pytest suite together, expect 429 rate-limit errors on /auth/login (throttle:20,1) — run each test file separately or wait 60s between runs. Draft AFS UI conditionally renders only afs-send-{id}; afs-sign-{id} and afs-register-{id} appear after the status transitions (this is correct product behaviour, verified by backend test test_afs_full_lifecycle).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Two minor testing artifacts: (1) Playwright modal close via Escape didn't dismiss the pay modal (modal-overlay intercepted subsequent clicks); worked around by scoping AFS UI check to a separate session. (2) Login throttle interferes with the full pytest -n auto regression run; not an app bug.
